dialect.detail: Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC) COBOL for DECSYSTEM-20; uses DEC-specific extensions including DISPLAY-7 usage clause, RMS INDEXED file organization, COMP-1 floating point, and DIL (Data Interchange Library) interface routines for VAX/DEC-20 interoperability
evidence: CALL DILINI, CALL ROPEN, CALL RCLOSE, CALL RWRITE, CALL CVGEN

purpose.domain_detail: DEC DIL (Data Interchange Library) Load Test sample application; reads a local RMS indexed file on DEC-20 and writes a remote sequential ASCII file on a VAX system via DAP (Data Access Protocol) network routines
purpose.summary: JTVRPT is a DEC-20 COBOL program that is part of the DIL Load Test sample application. It opens a local RMS indexed job-ticket file, reads records sequentially, converts each record from SIXBIT to ASCII-7 using the DIL CVGEN routine, and writes the converted records to a remote sequential file on a VAX system via network DAP calls (ROPEN/RWRITE/RCLOSE). It includes detailed error handling for both DIL and DIX status codes.

notable_features: RMS INDEXED file organization with RECORD KEY
COPY from SYS:DIL.LIB (DIX, DIT, DIL copybooks)
CALL to DIL routines: DILINI, ROPEN, RCLOSE, RWRITE, CVGEN
Data conversion between SIXBIT (DEC-10/20) and ASCII-7 (VAX)
Network remote file access via DAP protocol
Detailed DIL/DIX error message handling sections
OCCURS 10 in file record for detail lines
VALUE OF IDENTIFICATION IS file label clause
verdict.notes: This is a well-documented DEC COBOL sample/test application from 1982-1984 with a full edit history. The source format appears fixed-column but the mechanical indicator says 'unknown' likely due to tab indentation in some areas. The program contains a commented-out line ('*    PERFORM OPEN-REMOTE-FILE') and a 'perform main' that references a MAIN SECTION, suggesting the open/write flow was restructured during development. The DIX-C-IMPOSSIBLE message contains an expletive in the display string, consistent with internal DEC engineering code of the era.
